project.name: Longforgan
project.boundarySource: Verified named-place position with a conservative strict editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Completed as an individual, strict-boundary audit on 2026-09-02. Nearby attractions and facilities are excluded unless they lie inside the defined visitor study area.

touristAppeal.label: Notable Stop
touristAppeal.summary: Longforgan clears the map threshold through its coherent historic core, mercat cross, church with limited visitor opening, community café session and local core paths. Restricted opening and modest all-day facilities keep it a notable stop rather than a destination.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Outdoor access is useful with responsible close control; indoor policies must be checked separately.

visitorHighlights.name: Longforgan Parish Church
visitorHighlights.reason: The church and historic core form a coherent short stop, not a full-day destination.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Wednesdays, May to August, 14:00–16:00; also by arrangement.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A genuine in-boundary visitor place assessed separately from settlement-level appeal.

townGuide.headline: A fully audited notable stop
townGuide.intro: Longforgan clears the map threshold through its coherent historic core, mercat cross, church with limited visitor opening, community café session and local core paths. Restricted opening and modest all-day facilities keep it a notable stop rather than a destination.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Use the verified cards only
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: The guide excludes neighbouring attractions and unverified facilities.

townStudyArea.sourceName: Verified named-place position with a conservative strict editorial study buffer
townStudyArea.notes: Longforgan has no separate NRS locality polygon in the reference dataset. The published editorial boundary is therefore the strict heritage study area; the 500 m ring is context only.

features.name: Longforgan Parish Church
features.shortDescription: Historic parish church with a 1690 tower, 1795 main body, medieval stones and limited summer visitor opening.

sourceRecords.sourceName: Longforgan Parish Church
sourceRecords.licence: Source-linked editorial evidence; check time-sensitive details before travel.
sourceRecords.notes: Current trust page gives construction history, seasonal Wednesday opening and visitor toilet provision during opening.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A genuine in-boundary visitor place assessed separately from settlement-level appeal.

attractionGuide.headline: Nine centuries of Carse worship
attractionGuide.intro: The church and historic core form a coherent short stop, not a full-day destination.
attractionGuide.parking: Huntly Wood has a small separately audited public car park; do not assume church forecourt parking.
attractionGuide.toilets: An accessible toilet is available during church opening only.
attractionGuide.picnic: No formal picnic facility is claimed.
attractionGuide.foodNote: The church hall hosts a Wednesday-morning Pop-in Café when advertised.

sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact boundary intersection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: The spatial layer supplies designation and location, not a historic construction period. Undated records remain in the catalogue but are hidden from the heat map.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland NRHE / trove.scot Points GIS
sources.coverage: NRHE records whose representative points lie within the authoritative Longforgan parish extent
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact parish containment
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: The spatial index provides a representative site point, names and classifications. It does not establish construction dates; detailed source records require individual review.

sources.name: Historic Environment Scotland Listed Buildings spatial data
sources.coverage: Longforgan editorial district plus 500m heritage buffer; buffer records are retained as related context
sources.accessMethod: Developer-supplied local HES Shapefile; exact polygon selection
sources.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
sources.limitations: Longforgan has no separate NRS locality boundary. The transparent visitor-guide editorial boundary is used and buffer records remain context only. The source supplies statutory designation and location metadata, not construction dates.

sources.name: Longforgan identity and strict audit boundary
sources.accessMethod: Named-place identity and boundary-aware editorial review
sources.limitations: The boundary is an editorial visitor study area, not an administrative claim.
